frozen_required_deliverable: A detector that compares a run against the committed tree with a run against a pristine export of the same commit and reports any behavioural divergence as hidden-state dependence.

vacuity_probe.method: Forced the divergence decision to a constant in both directions and re-ran the producer's own tests.
vacuity_probe.conclusion: Not vacuous, and notably the suite pins BOTH directions: it carries a real negative control (test_equivalent_behavior_is_not_misclassified), so a detector that always fires is also rejected.

hidden_cases.rationale: The producer only tested hidden state supplied as an UNTRACKED file. The more common real form is a locally MODIFIED tracked file, which the producer's tests never cover.
hidden_cases.construction: committed probe.py printing 'committed-version'; working tree copy overwritten to print 'locally-modified'; detector run against HEAD.
hidden_cases.observed_output_verbatim: HC-C exit: 1 hidden_state_dependence: True warm: 'locally-modified\n' pristine: 'committed-version\n'
hidden_cases.interpretation: True positive. git archive of the commit correctly ignores the working-tree modification, so the detector generalises beyond the untracked-file case the producer tested.

hidden_cases.rationale: Adversarial precision probe: the warm run executes in the repository directory and the pristine run executes in a differently-named export directory. Any command whose output legitimately reflects its own location will diverge for reasons that are not hidden-state dependence.
hidden_cases.construction: committed probe.py containing 'import os; print(os.path.basename(os.getcwd()))'; NO uncommitted state whatsoever.
hidden_cases.observed_output_verbatim:
HC-A exit: 1 hidden_state_dependence: True
HC-A warm stdout: 'cwdrepo\n' pristine stdout: 'exp1\n'
hidden_cases.interpretation: FALSE POSITIVE. The detector reports hidden-state dependence on a repository that has none. Root cause: compare() decides divergence by raw equality of the whole {returncode, stdout, stderr} triple, and the two runs are structurally guaranteed to differ in working-directory name.

hidden_cases.rationale: Second precision probe: nondeterministic but entirely committed behaviour.
hidden_cases.construction: committed probe.py containing 'import random; print(random.random())'; no uncommitted state.
hidden_cases.observed_output_verbatim: HC-B exit: 1 hidden_state_dependence: True (no uncommitted state exists)
hidden_cases.interpretation: FALSE POSITIVE. Any nondeterministic command output is misreported as hidden-state dependence. Unit 005 in the same cohort explicitly normalises nondeterminism out before comparing; this unit does not.

producer_declared_limitations: Comparison covers supplied-command exit code, stdout, and stderr; behaviorally inert hidden state is not reported.
scope_honesty_assessment.assessment: The producer honestly declared its FALSE-NEGATIVE boundary (behaviourally inert hidden state) but declared no FALSE-POSITIVE boundary, and HC-A/HC-B show a broad one: cwd-sensitive output and nondeterministic output are both misreported as hidden-state dependence with zero uncommitted state present. Because the two runs execute in different directories by construction, HC-A is not an exotic edge case. This is an undeclared precision limitation, not an invented claim.
scope_honesty_assessment.does_it_refute_the_frozen_hypothesis: No. The frozen hypothesis asserts that hidden-state dependence 'can be detected mechanically rather than by inspection' - a detectability (soundness) claim, and I confirmed detection on both the untracked-file case and my own modified-tracked-file case with zero false negatives observed. Precision is not part of the frozen wording. I therefore reach PASS on the hypothesis while recording the undeclared false-positive class as a mandatory limitation addendum.

reproducibility_check: Producer tests and all three hidden cases were run in fresh python3 -I processes and were stable on repeat.
disposition_reason: All eight frozen criteria are independently satisfied, the tests are non-vacuous in BOTH directions (a real negative control is present), and the detector shows genuine detection power beyond what the producer tested - my modified-tracked-file case (HC-C) was correctly caught. Accepted subject to one mandatory limitation addendum: the detector has an undeclared false-positive class (HC-A cwd-sensitive output, HC-B nondeterministic output), which matters because the warm and pristine runs execute in differently-named directories by construction. That is a precision defect, not a soundness defect, and the frozen hypothesis is a detectability claim, so it does not warrant rejection.
followups_for_coordinator: hidden_state_detector.compare() decides divergence by raw equality of the whole {returncode, stdout, stderr} triple. Reviewer-observed false positives: a committed command printing os.getcwd() basename, and a committed command printing random.random(), are both reported as hidden_state_dependence=true with no uncommitted state present. The producer's declared limitations cover only false negatives; the false-positive class should be declared or normalised out (unit 005 does normalise).
